verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              तस्मिन्प्रविष्टे दुर्धर्षे सृञ्जयानमितौजसि।  अमृष्यमाणे संरब्धे का वोऽभूद्वै मतिस्तदा॥१॥
दुर्योधनं तथा पुत्रमुक्त्वा शास्त्रातिगं मम।  यत्प्राविशदमेयात्मा किं पार्थः प्रत्यपद्यत॥२॥
verses.english: Having addressed my disobedient son Duryodhana thus, when that of immeasurable energy entered into the Pandava army) what did Partha do?

verses.sanskrit: निहते सैन्धवे वीरे भूरिश्रवसि चैव ह।  यदाभ्यगान्महातेजाः पञ्चालानपराजितः॥३॥
verses.english: (You say that) on the slaughter of the heroic king of Sindhu as well as of Bhurisrava that unvanquished one (i.e., Drona) endued with great energy rushed against the Srinjayas.

verses.sanskrit: किममन्यत दुर्धर्षे प्रविष्टे शत्रुतापने।  दुर्योधनस्तु किं कृत्यं प्राप्तकालममन्यत॥४॥
के च तं वरदं वीरमन्वयुर्द्विजसत्तमम्।  के चास्य पृष्ठतोऽगच्छन् वीराः शूरस्य युध्यतः॥५॥
verses.english: Who were they that followed the heroic bestower of boons, the foremost of the twiceborn ones? Who, O charioteer, were the warriors that remained behind that fighting hero?

verses.sanskrit: के पुरस्ताद्वर्तन्त निघ्नन्तः शात्रवान् रणे।  मन्येऽहं पाण्डवान् सर्वान् भारद्वाजशरार्दितान्॥६॥
verses.english: Who were they that fought in, his van when he was destroying the enemies? I think that afflicted with the darts of the of Bharadvaja, all the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: शिशिरे कंपमाना वै कृशा गाव इव प्रभो। प्रविश्य स महेष्वासः पञ्चालानरिमर्दनः।  कथं तु पुरुषव्याघ्रः पञ्चत्वमुपजग्मिवान्॥७॥
verses.english: Like lean cows shivering in cold. Having entered into the Panchalas how that mighty wielder of bow, that grinder of foes and foremost of men came by his end?

verses.sanskrit: सर्वेषु योधेषु च सङ्गतेषु रात्रौ समेतेषु महारथेषु।  संलोड्यमानेषु पृथग्बलेषु के वस्तदानीं मतिमन्त आसन्॥८॥
हतांश्चैव विषक्तांश्च पराभूतांश्च शंससि।  रथिनो विरथांश्चैव कृतान्युद्धेषु मामकान्॥९॥
verses.english: son (You say) that, in the encounter. my soldiers were (either) killed, Driven away or defeated and that my car-warriors were deprived of their cars in the encounter.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां संलोड्यमानानां पाण्डवैर्हतचेतसाम्।  अन्धे तमसि मग्नानामभवत्का मतिस्तदा॥१०॥
verses.english: Crushed and deprived of senses by the Pandavas and buried in blinding darkness (as they were), what was (the state of) their mind?

verses.sanskrit: प्रहृष्टांश्चाप्युदग्रांश्च संतुष्टांश्चैव पाण्डवान्।  शंससीहाप्रहृष्टांश्च विभ्रष्टांश्चैव मामकान्॥११॥
verses.english: You say that the Pandavas were full of joy and elated (with success) and that my partisans were cheerless, heartless and struck with terror,

verses.sanskrit: कथमेषां तदा तत्र पार्थानामपलायिनाम्।  प्रकाशमभवद्रात्रौ कथं कुरुषु सञ्जय॥१२॥

सञ्जय उवाच।
              रात्रियुद्धे तदा राजन्वर्तमाने सुदारुणे।  द्रोणमभ्यद्रवन्सर्वे पाण्डवाः सह सोमकैः॥१३॥
ततो द्रोणः केकयांश्च धृष्टद्युम्नस्य चात्मजान्।  संप्रैषयत्प्रेतलोकं सर्वानिषुभिराशुगैः॥१४॥
verses.english: But Drona, by means of his swift-going darts, sent the Kekayas and sons of Dhrishtadyumna to the region of the departed spirits.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य मुष्टिहतस्याजौ पाण्डवेन बलीयसा।  सर्वाण्यस्थीनि सहसा प्रापतन्वै पृथक् पृथक्॥१४॥
verses.english: But Drona, by means of his swift-going darts, sent the Kekayas and sons of Dhrishtadyumna to the region of the departed spirits.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य प्रमुखतो राजन् येऽवर्तन्त महारथाः।  तान्सर्वान्प्रेषयामास पितृलोकं स भारत॥१५॥
प्रमथ्नन्तं तदा वीरान्भारद्वाजं महारथम्।  अभ्यवर्तत संक्रुद्धः शिबी राजा प्रतापवान्॥१६॥
तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य पाण्डवानां महारथम्।  विव्याध दशभिर्बाणैः सर्वपारशवैः शितैः॥१७॥
verses.english: Secing the great car-warrior of the Pandavas advance, Drona pierced him with ten arrows made wholly of steel.

verses.sanskrit: तं शिबिः प्रतिविव्याध त्रिंशता निशितैः शरैः।  सारथिं चास्य भल्लेन स्मयमानो न्यपातयत्॥१८॥
तस्य द्रोणो हयान्हत्वा सारथिं च महात्मनः।  अथास्य सशिरस्त्राणं शिरः कायादपाहरत्॥१९॥
verses.english: (On the other hand) Drona, having killed the horses as well as the charioteer of that highsouled one, severed his head, adorned with a diadem, from the body.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽस्य सारथिं क्षिप्रमन्यं दुर्योधनोऽदिशत्।  स तेन संगृहीताश्वः पुनरभ्यद्रवद्रिपून्॥२०॥
verses.english: Duryodhana then quickly ordered charioteer (to guide Drona's car). The reins of the) horses being taken by him, he (i.c., Drona) again proceeded against his foes.

verses.sanskrit: कलिङ्गानामनीकेन कालिङ्गस्य सुतो रणे।  पूर्वं पितृवधात्क्रुद्धो भीमसेनसुपाद्रवत्॥२१॥
verses.english: Accompanied by the Kalinga forces the son of the king of Kalinga, excited with wrath for the destruction of his father by Bhimasena, rushed towards him.

verses.sanskrit: स भीमं पञ्चभिर्विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध सप्तभिः।  विशोकं त्रिभिरानर्च्छत् ध्वजमेकेन पत्त्रिणा॥२२॥
कलिङ्गानां तु तं शूरं क्रुद्धं क्रुद्धो वृकोदरः।  रथाद्रथमभिद्रुत्य मुष्टिनाऽभिजघान ह॥२३॥
तं कर्णो भ्रातरश्चास्य नामृष्यन्त परंतप।  ते भीमसेनं नाराचैर्जघ्नुराशीविषोपमैः॥२५॥
verses.english: Karna and all the brothers (of the Kalinga prince) could not bear that act of the part of Bhimasena. They (therefore) struck him with keen darts (as fierce) as poisonous snakes.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शत्रुरथं त्यक्ता भीमो ध्रुवरथं गतः। ध्रुवं चास्यन्तमनिशं मुष्टिना समपोथयत्॥२६॥
verses.english: Bhima, then leaving the car of his enemy (i.e., dead Kalinga prince) made for the car of Dhruva and smashed Dhruva who was incessantly striking him, by a blow of his fist.

verses.sanskrit: स तथा पाण्डुपुत्रेण बलिनाऽभिहतोऽपतत्।  तं निहत्य महाराज भीमसेनो महाबलः॥२७॥
verses.english: Thus struck by the powerful son of Pandu, he fell down (from his car). The highly powerful Bhimasena, Oking, after slaying him.

verses.sanskrit: जयरातरथं प्राप्य मुहुः सिंह इवानदत्।  जयरातमथाक्षिप्य नदन्सव्येन पाणिना॥२८॥
verses.english: Got up to the car of Jayadratha and repeatedly sent forth leoninc roars. While roaring he hurled him down with his left hand.

verses.sanskrit: तलेन नाशयामास कर्णस्यैवाग्रतः स्थितः।  कर्णस्तु पाण्डवे शक्तिं काञ्चनीं समवासृजत्॥२९॥
verses.english: And he (then) killed him with a slap in the very presence of Karna himself. Karna then shot a golden dart at that Pandava.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तामेव जग्राह प्रहसन्पाण्डुनन्दनः।  कर्णायैव च दुर्धर्षश्चिक्षेपाजौ वृकोदरः॥३०॥
verses.english: But the son of Pandu seized that (dart) with a smile. And in that encounter the invincible Vrikodara hurled that very dart of Karna.

verses.sanskrit: तामापतन्तीं चिच्छेद शकुनिस्तैलपायिना।  एतत्कृत्वा महत्कर्म रणेऽद्भुतपराक्रमः॥३१॥
verses.english: (Then) Shakuni cut-off that dart while it was coming (towards Karna) by a shaft saturated with oil. Having performed such great exploits in battle, that one of marvellous prowess.

verses.sanskrit: पुनः स्वरथमास्थाय दुद्राव तव वाहिनीम्। तमायान्तं जिघांसन्तं भीमं क्रुद्धमिवान्तकम्॥३२॥
verses.english: Returned to his own car and (then) rushed against your troops. When Bhima desirous of staying (your troops), was (thus) advancing furiously like the (grim) destroyer himself.

verses.sanskrit: न्यवारयन्महाबाहुं तव पुत्रा विशांपते।  महता शरवर्षेण च्छादयन्तो महारथाः॥३३॥
verses.english: Your mighty armed-sons, those great carwarriors tried to check his career by enveloping him with mighty showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्मदस्तु ततो भीमः प्रहसन्निव संयुगे।  सारथिं च ह्ययांश्चैव शरैर्निन्ये यमक्षयम्॥३४॥
दुर्मदस्तु ततो यानं दुष्कर्णस्यावचक्रमे।  तावेकरथमारूढौ भ्रातरौ परतापनौ॥३५॥
verses.english: Durmada then got to the car of Duskarna. Those two brothers, the tormentors of foes, mounted on the same car.

verses.sanskrit: संग्रामशिरसो मध्ये भीमं द्वावप्यधावताम्।  यथाम्बुपतिमित्रौ हि तारकं दैत्यसत्तमम्॥३६॥
verses.english: Both rushed against Bhima in the van of the battle, as the lord of the water (i.e. Varuna) (had rushed against) Taraka, the foremost of the Daitayas (in days of yore).

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु दुर्मदश्चैव दुष्कर्णश्च तवात्मजौ।  रथमेकं समारुह्य भीमं बाणैरविध्यताम्॥३७॥
verses.english: Then your sons Durmada and Duskarna ascending the same car pierced Bhima with arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कर्णस्य मिषतो द्रौणेर्दुर्योधनस्य च।  कृपस्य सोमदत्तस्य बाल्हीकस्य च पाण्डवः॥३८॥
दुर्मदस्य च वीरस्य दुष्कर्णस्य च तं रथम्।  पादप्रहारेण धरां प्रावेशयदरिन्दिमः॥३९॥
verses.english: That chastiser of foes, buried the car of the heroic Durmada and that of Duskarna into the earth with the stroke of his foot.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सुतौ ते बलिनौ शूरौ दुष्कर्णदुर्मदौ।  मुष्टिनाऽऽहत्य संक्रुद्धो ममर्द च ननर्द च॥४०॥
verses.english: Then striking furiously with the blows of his fits those two heroic and powerful sons of yours, Duskama and Durmada, he crushed them (therewith) and sent forth thundering shouts.

verses.sanskrit: ततो हाहाकृते सैन्ये दृष्ट्वा भीमं नृपाऽब्रुवन्।  रुद्रोऽयं भीमरूपेण धार्तराष्ट्रेषु युध्यति॥४१॥
verses.english: Then your troops began to wail aloud and the kings seeing Bhima, said. "He is Rudra himself who assuming the shape of a Bhima is fighting with the troops of Dhritarashtra.”

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा पलायन्ते सर्वे भारत पार्थिवाः।  विसंज्ञा वाहयन्वाहान्न च द्वौ सह धावतः॥४२॥
verses.english: 0 Bharata, saying this, all the kings deprived, (as it were) of their senses and urging the animals (on which they rode), fled away (from the field) and no two then (so great was their terror) did run together.

verses.sanskrit: ततो बले भृशलुलिते निशामुखे सुपूजितो नृपवृषभैर्वृकोदरः।  महाबलः कमलविबुद्धलोचनो युधिष्ठिरं नृपतिमपूजयद्बली॥४३॥
verses.english: The army (of the Kurus) being thus greatly crushed, in that night, the heroic and highly powerful Vrikodara, endued with full blown lotus-like eyes, being highly complemented by (many) foremost of kings, paid his regards to king Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: ततो यमौ द्रुपद-विराट-केकया युधिष्ठिरश्चापि परां मुदं ययुः।  वृकोदरं भृशमनुपूजयंश्च ते यथाऽन्धके प्रतिनिहते हरं सुराः॥४४॥
ततः सुतास्ते वरुणात्मजोपमा रुषान्विताः सह गुरुणा महात्मना। वृकोदरं सरथपदातिकुञ्जरा युयुत्सवो भृशमभिपर्यवारयन्॥४५॥
verses.english: Then your sons resembling those of Varuna filled with wrath and eager for battle led by (their) high-souled preceptor surrounded on all sides Vrikodara by cars foot-soldiers and clephants.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽभवत्तिमिरघनैरिवावृते महाभये भयदमतीव दारुणम्।  निशामुखे वृकबलगृध्रमोदनं महात्मनां नृपवरयुद्धमद्भुतम्॥४६॥
verses.english: Then, O best of kings, on that dreadful night enveloped with darkness thick as clouds, there took place, between those high-souled ones, an awe-inspiring and terrible battle delightful to wolves, crows and vultures.
